architecture.mechanism: The paper models the joint influence of motor behavior and inverter dynamics to assess power electro-mechanical and conversion losses under realistic operating conditions, revealing efficiency variations and loss distribution across driving cycles.
architecture.intervention: Port the integrated motor-inverter loss/efficiency model into the Silverado 1500's battery electrical system as an onboard health monitor: compute expected conversion losses during 60 mph cruise, compare against measured losses, and when abnormal loss distribution signals incipient battery thermal failure, command load-shedding/derating that prioritizes ABS, stability control, traction control, and braking power feeds.
architecture.expected_effect: Early detection of thermal-driven electrical malfunction before cascade, plus graceful power management that preserves braking and vehicle control at highway speeds during battery failure.
architecture.falsification_test: Instrument a 2019 Silverado 1500 to log battery temperature, motor/inverter losses, and ABS/stability-control warning events across repeated 60 mph highway runs; if predicted loss distribution does not statistically correlate with measured battery thermal rise and subsequent malfunction onset, the mechanism is falsified.
